name: Food Truck Revenue
description: Size the annual revenue of a single food truck parked on weekdays.
formula: Revenue = Annual weekday lunch-hour foot traffic x % nearby x % who buy x orders per visit x price per order
solution_logic: Step 1: Identify nearby traffic = target_population x addressable_segment
Step 2: Apply purchase rate = nearby_traffic x penetration_rate
Step 3: Calculate spend per purchase = purchase_frequency x avg_spend_per_purchase
Step 4: Calculate annual revenue = buyers x spend_per_purchase
key_insight: This is a single truck at a single spot, weekdays only -- the whole estimate has to be built up from lunch-hour foot traffic at this one location, not narrowed down from a city's food-service market.
common_mistakes: Sizing the citywide food truck or restaurant market instead of this one truck's lunch-hour foot traffic
Forgetting that this is weekdays only and accidentally scaling as if the truck operates 7 days a week
Treating everyone near the truck at lunch as a buyer instead of applying both a notice filter and a purchase filter
framework_soundbite: One truck, weekday lunch traffic only, two filters before you multiply by price -- nothing here comes from a city population.
business_contexts: a food truck owner deciding whether a new parking spot is worth the permit cost
a food truck startup pitching investors on a single-truck pilot
question_patterns: A food truck startup is deciding whether a downtown lunch spot is worth a year-long parking permit and wants a bottom-up revenue estimate first.

target_population.unit: people/year (weekday lunch-hour foot traffic near the spot)

addressable_segment.unit: % close enough to the truck during lunch

prompts.beginner: Estimate the annual revenue of a single food truck parked in a downtown business district on weekdays.
prompts.intermediate: A food truck startup is deciding whether a downtown lunch spot is worth a year-long parking permit and wants a bottom-up revenue estimate first.
prompts.advanced: A food truck operator has one truck and is choosing between renewing a downtown weekday permit or trying a new neighborhood with unproven foot traffic. Before deciding, they want a defensible bottom-up revenue estimate for the current spot, built from lunch-hour foot traffic, not a citywide estimate.

approach_guidance.bottom_up_why: Start from the lunch-hour foot traffic actually near this one truck on the days it operates, filter down to who's close enough and who buys, then multiply by what they spend -- there's no larger market to narrow down from, just this one spot.
